Plot survival along a record of temperature

Source: R/plot-survival.R
plot_survival.Rd

Draws the survival predicted by predict_survival() or average_survival(): the probability of surviving to each time of the record, as the posterior median with its credible interval. The result is a ggplot object, to be refined by the user with further ggplot2 layers, scales, labels and themes.

Usage

plot_survival(
  x,
  temperature = FALSE,
  facet = TRUE,
  colour_by = NULL,
  interval = is.null(colour_by),
  time_unit = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A list, the output of predict_survival() or average_survival().

temperature

A single logical value, whether to draw the record of temperature, and of any co-stressor that changes along it, in panels above the survival curve. Defaults to FALSE.

facet

A single logical value or the character string "all". TRUE (the default) gives a panel per setting of newdata, cut down to quartile values when there are many; "all" a panel for every setting; FALSE no panels, with a colour per setting.

colour_by

An optional character string naming a numeric covariate of newdata, to colour the curves by.

interval

A single logical value, whether to draw the credible interval. Defaults to TRUE, and to FALSE with colour_by.

time_unit

An optional character string giving the time unit for the axis label, e.g. "min". The fit does not record the unit of its times, so none is shown unless given.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

By default each setting of newdata has its own panel, following the same rule as in plot_tdt(). There are two ways to draw the settings together in one panel. With facet = FALSE each setting has its own colour, from teal to deep purple in the order of newdata, and an entry in the legend, which suits a few settings or a covariate that is not numeric; with more than eight settings the colours are too close to tell apart, and a message says to use panels or colour_by. With colour_by, the curves of every value of one numeric covariate are coloured on a continuous scale from teal for its lowest value to deep purple for its highest, and the intervals are left out by default, since they overlap.

With temperature = TRUE the record of temperature is drawn above the survival curve on the same time axis, so that a drop in survival can be read against the temperatures that caused it. A co-stressor the record follows through time is drawn in a panel of its own between the two, named by its column, when it changes along the record; one that stays constant is left out.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# a model fitted to a small ramping trial: 20 individuals warmed from 20 to 35
# degrees over 60 minutes and checked every minute, in two trials (see fit_hazard())
path   <- data.frame(path_id = "A", time = c(0, 60), temp = c(20, 35))
checks <- data.frame(path_id = "A", time = seq(0, 60, by = 1))
ind    <- data.frame(id = 1:20, path_id = "A", event = 1, mass = runif(20, 8, 12),
                     trial = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 10),
                     t_upper = sample(seq(10, 60, 10), 20, replace = TRUE))
long   <- build_hazard_data(ind, path, "interval", covariates = c("mass", "trial"),
                            checks = checks)
fit    <- fit_hazard(long, "exp", dpar_formulas = list(loga = ~ 1 + mass))
# a two-day record read every hour, with a daily cycle
hours  <- 0:48
record <- data.frame(time = hours * 60, day = pmin(hours %/% 24, 1),
                     temp = 24 + 3 * sin(2 * pi * (hours - 9) / 24))

pred <- predict_survival(fit, record, newdata = data.frame(mass = c(8, 12)))
plot_survival(pred, time_unit = "min")
plot_survival(pred, temperature = TRUE, time_unit = "min")

# both masses in one panel, the record drawn once
plot_survival(pred, temperature = TRUE, facet = FALSE, time_unit = "min")
} # }
